issues.description: `PreemptDisabled` is changed from an uninhabited guardian backed by `DisabledPreemptGuard` into a constructible unit struct whose guard constructors return `()`, so taking a lock no longer establishes or retains the advertised preemption-disabled state.
issues.rationale: The reviewed revision makes `PreemptDisabled` a public unit struct and binds both `SpinGuardian::Guard` and `ReadGuard` to `()`. Its constructors return unit instead of calling `disable_preempt`, despite the trait/type documentation promising a guardian that maintains atomic mode by disabling preemption while a lock is held. This changes executable lock behavior and permits construction of the guardian marker without the original zero-variant restriction. Collaborator rikosellic explicitly objects to changing the guard struct/function definitions and asks to preserve them while using Verus external annotations. The direct child commit restores `DisabledPreemptGuard` as both associated types and calls `disable_preempt` from externally verified constructors; the final child restores the zero-variant `PreemptDisabled` enum via `external_type_specification`. The exact repair sequence confirms that the unit-returning historical implementation was not an acceptable abstraction of the runtime guard.
issues.verification: Source and Git-history adjudication; historical Verus not executed. Selected the latest official PR commit before the modification request, verified its true merge-base, inspected the unit-returning guardian implementation, and compared both direct repair commits. The archived final head contains the repair and therefore is not relabeled.
